description: Ex-USAAF 44-76339 and ex-RAAF A65-73; later civil VH-CIP. Under restoration as a static display and the museum's landmark aircraft; formerly displayed outside the Beck Museum at Mareeba. Source: FNQ Aviation Museum website and The Express (Mareeba), 18 February 2026.

Empire Air Training Scheme-era trainer on display; the museum is seeking propeller parts for it. Identity not published. Source: FNQ Aviation Museum website and The Express (Mareeba), 18 February 2026.

First flight 29/09/1954, delivered 04/11/1954, approved for disposal 19/11/1971 and sold 12/04/1972. Long displayed in the Sid Beck Collection at Mareeba; reported in February 2026 as recently acquired by the FNQ Aviation Museum, also at Mareeba. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials. Source: FNQ Aviation Museum website and The Express (Mareeba), 18 February 2026.

Used by ARDU for high Mach number Vampire testing, then Instructional Vampire Airframe No. 11 at RSTT Wagga. Bought by a Brisbane scrap yard that intended to pole-mount it, then acquired by Syd Beck. Long displayed in the Beck Collection at Mareeba and reported in February 2026 as recently acquired by the FNQ Aviation Museum. Identity and current holder confirmed on ADF-Serials. Source: FNQ Aviation Museum website and The Express (Mareeba), 18 February 2026.

Wing section and fragments recovered from the crash site of the B-17E known as Hoomalimali, displayed as a relic rather than a preserved airframe; the USAAF serial was not established. Source: FNQ Aviation Museum website and The Express (Mareeba), 18 February 2026.
